item.title: Brandon Paul breaks down after TikTok star MacKenzie Paul dies at 26 following three year battle with acute myeloid leukaemia
item.description: TikTok star MacKenzie Paul has died at 26 after a three-year fight with acute myeloid leukemia. Her husband, Brandon Paul, confirmed her death in an emotional Facebook video. According to People Magazine, MacKenzie became known for sharing her cancer journey openly, inspiring thousands before her passing
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Jessica Daugirdas dies at 35 after sharing her three-year colorectal cancer fight with followers
item.description: Jessica Daugirdas, a Brazilian influencer, died at 35 after a three-year fight with colorectal cancer. Her family confirmed her death on Instagram on January 25. Known for sharing her health journey online, Jessica inspired thousands with her honesty, strength, and faith while facing cancer and its many challenges.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Border Patrol commander Gregory Bovino removed amid backlash over Pretti shooting; Kristi Noem also said to be at risk: Report
item.description: US Border Patrol's "commander at large," Gregory Bovino, has been removed following the fatal shooting of a US citizen by agents under his command. This demotion signals a potential shift in the Trump administration's aggressive immigration enforcement tactics. President Trump and Minnesota Governor Walz have also adopted a more conciliatory tone after a call regarding the deportation drive.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Big armada’ near Iran: Trump says Tehran 'wants to talk, strike deal' amid rising tensions
item.description: President Trump announced a "big armada" is deployed near Iran, stating the situation remains in flux. While close to ordering strikes earlier this month, he delayed the decision, believing Tehran genuinely seeks a deal. The US has bolstered its military presence in the region, including an aircraft carrier strike group, as diplomatic options are also being considered.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Alert: UK households urged to stockpile three essentials ahead of Storm Chandra power cut risk
item.description: Storm Chandra is set to bring disruptive weather across the UK from late Monday into Tuesday, with heavy rain, strong winds and snow triggering multiple Met Office warnings. Flooding is likely in parts of southern England, while northern England and Scotland face hill snow and travel disruption. Households are urged to prepare for possible power cuts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: West Virginia woman arrested in alleged Trump assassination plot; sheriff says she recruit people on social media
item.description: A West Virginia woman, Morgan Morrow, faces charges for allegedly attempting to recruit individuals to assassinate President Donald Trump. Authorities apprehended Morrow after discovering a TikTok post where she seemingly solicited a sniper. She reportedly admitted to posting the message, citing personal reasons for her animosity towards the President.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: YouTuber WhistlinDiesel faces another tax arrest after previous 2025 case
item.description: Popular YouTuber WhistlinDiesel, Cody Detwiler, was arrested again for a $30,000 tax dispute, claiming he received no prior notice. This follows a previous tax evasion arrest in November 2025. Detwiler stated the issue stems from a vehicle registered in Montana that was later destroyed, leading to a prolonged tax case without official notification.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: MrBeast criticizes Netflix pay, would give Alex Honnold over $500K for Taipei 101 stunt
item.description: Daredevil Alex Honnold's breathtaking free solo of Taipei 101 has sparked a bidding war, with YouTuber MrBeast claiming he'd have paid over $500,000 for the stunt on his platform. Honnold's 90-minute climb, broadcast live on Netflix, highlights the growing appeal of extreme urban feats and the fierce competition between streaming giants for high-stakes entertainment.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: WATCH: iShowSpeed pulls off dangerous backflip at Ghana’s Black Star Square during live stream
item.description: American streamer iShowSpeed thrilled fans by performing a daring backflip next to Ghana's Black Star monument on January 26, 2026. The stunt occurred during his Africa tour's final show at Black Star Square, showcasing his adventurous streaming style. While fans celebrated his bravery, the risky move near the historical landmark also sparked safety concerns.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: ‘Stay away from USA’: Former FIFA chief Sepp Blatter fuels World Cup 2026 boycott debate
item.description: Amidst rising geopolitical tensions and concerns over US policies, a growing chorus is calling for a boycott of the 2026 FIFA World Cup co-hosted by the United States. Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter has publicly supported calls for fans to stay away, citing recent incidents and the perceived contradiction with the tournament's spirit of unity.

item.title: Did Tim Walz ask Donald Trump to work together? Minnesota governor, US president have ‘productive’ call over ICE protests
item.description: Following the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti by a Border Patrol agent, Minnesota Governor Tim Walz and President Trump held a "productive" call. Trump agreed to allow the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension to investigate the incident and to review reducing federal agent numbers in the state.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Russia to hire 40,000 Indian workers in 2026, paying up to $1,000 amid labour shortage: Report
item.description: In a bold move to tackle its acute labor shortage, Russia is gearing up to welcome more than 40,000 Indian workers by 2026. This strategic decision comes in the wake of demographic challenges and an ongoing conflict, underlining the need for skilled labor. Following a recent mobility agreement, many Indian professionals are already contributing to the Russian workforce.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'I can handle it': Mark Carney shrugs off Donald Trump’s ‘Governor’ jibe amid 100% tariff threat
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney dismissed Donald Trump's 'Governor' remark, stating he can handle it. Trump, threatening a 100% tariff, accused Canada of becoming a 'Drop Off Port' for Chinese goods. Carney, while not commenting on every tweet, emphasized the importance of respecting Canadian troops amidst the escalating trade tensions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘No anaesthesia for MAGA’: Florida nurse refuses to treat Republicans, sparks calls for suspension
item.description: A Florida nurse named Erik Martindale has stirred up a storm on social media after declaring on Facebook that he would deny anesthesia to MAGA supporters. His bold statement has sparked outrage and prompted calls for the revocation of his nursing license. In a twist, Martindale later claimed his social media accounts had been compromised.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
